overview.headline: How population counts set House seats by equal proportions

keyPoints.point: Representatives are apportioned among the States with respective numbers counted by enumeration.
keyPoints.quote: Representatives and direct Taxes shall be apportioned among the several States which may be included within this Union

keyPoints.point: The Method of Equal Proportions adopted in 1941 assigns House seats using a priority value.
keyPoints.quote: The current method used, the Method of Equal Proportions, was adopted by congress in 1941 following the census of 1940.

keyPoints.point: Each of the 50 states is given one seat of the 435 total before remaining seats go by highest priority.
keyPoints.quote: Each of the 50 states is given one seat out of the current total of 435.

keyPoints.point: The multiplier is calculated with a divided value using the square root for each next seat number.
keyPoints.quote: 1 divided by the square root of n(n-1)

keyTerms.gloss: Assignment of House seats among states after population counting.
keyTerms.quote: Therein lies the primary mandate of the U.S. census, apportionment of the House of Representatives.

keyTerms.gloss: Number from multiplying state population by multiplier to rank next seats.
keyTerms.quote: The priority value is determined by multiplying the population of a state by a "multiplier."

keyTerms.gloss: Reciprocal factor used for calculating priority for each next seat.
